events.title: Isaac II Angelos kills Stephen Hagiochristophorites and raises a revolt
events.description: When Stephen Hagiochristophorites, lieutenant of Emperor Andronikos I Komnenos, tried to arrest him, Isaac II Angelos killed him and took refuge in the Hagia Sophia. His appeal to the people raised a revolt that deposed Andronikos and made Isaac emperor.

events.title: Wallace and Moray defeat the English at Stirling Bridge
events.description: Scottish forces under Andrew Moray and William Wallace destroyed an English army under the Earl of Surrey as it crossed the narrow bridge over the River Forth near Stirling. Moray was severely wounded and died later that year.
events.html: Scottish forces under Andrew Moray and William Wallace destroyed an English army under the Earl of Surrey as it crossed the narrow bridge over the River Forth near Stirling. Moray was severely wounded and died later that year.

events.title: The Teutonic Knights and Vytautas begin a siege of Vilnius
events.description: In the Lithuanian Civil War, the Teutonic Knights and their ally Vytautas began a five-week siege of Vilnius, whose castles were held by Skirgaila. The Knights ruined much of the outer city and destroyed the Crooked Castle but withdrew to Prussia.

events.title: Prince Eugene of Savoy destroys the Ottoman army at Zenta
events.description: Prince Eugene of Savoy surprised the Ottoman army of Sultan Mustafa II as it crossed the Tisza at Zenta and destroyed it, killing tens of thousands, including the grand vizier. The victory led to the Treaty of Karlowitz of 1699.

events.title: Marlborough wins a costly victory at Malplaquet
events.description: Marlborough and Prince Eugene drove a French army from its positions at Malplaquet, but lost far more men than the enemy. The bloodiest battle of the century strengthened calls in Britain for peace.
events.html: Marlborough and Prince Eugene drove a French army from its positions at Malplaquet, but lost far more men than the enemy. The bloodiest battle of the century strengthened calls in Britain for peace.

events.title: Howe defeats Washington at Brandywine
events.description: General William Howe outflanked Washington's army at Brandywine Creek in Pennsylvania. Two weeks later the British occupied Philadelphia, and Congress fled to York.

events.title: Ground is broken for the Pentagon
events.description: Construction began on the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, to house the War Department. Finished in just 16 months, it remains one of the world's largest office buildings.
events.html: Construction began on the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, to house the War Department. Finished in just 16 months, it remains one of the world's largest office buildings.

events.title: Military coup overthrows Chile's President Allende
events.description: Armed forces led by General Augusto Pinochet bombed the presidential palace, and Salvador Allende died inside. The US had worked to undermine Allende; Pinochet's dictatorship killed and disappeared thousands.
events.html: Armed forces led by General Augusto Pinochet bombed the presidential palace, and Salvador Allende died inside. The US had worked to undermine Allende; Pinochet's dictatorship killed and disappeared thousands.

events.title: Al-Qaeda's September 11 attacks kill 2,977 people
events.description: Hijackers crashed airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon; a fourth plane came down in Pennsylvania. The attacks killed 2,977 people and led to the US-led wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.
